## Saving results

**Publication tables &middot; Page 1**\
*The pages in this topic are numbered, and each builds on the ones before it,
starting with the results you save on this page.*

A publication-ready table in Word takes two steps. First, save the result of an
analysis under a name. R calls a saved result an *object*, and this page shows
how to make one. Second, give that object to `jtable()`, which writes the table
to a Word file. Page 2, [Making a table in Word](tables-in-word.qmd), shows that
step. For many readers those two pages are all they need. Each later page adds
one thing: several tables and a chart in one Word file (page 3), several results
side by side in one table (page 4), and a choice between the two table looks,
called *styles*, built into jstats (page 5). A second topic,
*Your own table styles*, picks up after page 5, for tables in a look you design
or a journal requires.

The Publication tables pages assume you can already run the analyses you'll put
in tables. They don't cover, for instance, how to choose the predictors for a
regression. What these pages cover is the step after the analysis, starting
here with saving its result. The page's last two blocks then save a result in a
file, so that a later session can use the result.

This page follows the pattern of every How-To: numbered blocks of code that
build one script, with the finished script to download at the bottom.
[Using the How-To pages](howtos.qmd#using-the-how-to-pages) explains the
pattern, and how to reset your session if something goes wrong.

### 1. Load jstats and the data

We'll work on `community`, one of the two practice datasets that ship with the
package: 103 simulated respondents to a community survey. `jload()` puts a copy
of it in your workspace, with the same command that loads a data file of your
own. `juse()` then makes `community` the default data frame, so the commands
that follow can leave its name out.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
.obx$show_console(r"---(## ---- 1. Load jstats and the data --------------------------------------

## Load jstats for this session
library(jstats)

## Load the community practice dataset into your workspace, then make it
## the default data frame, so the commands below can leave its name out
jload("community")
juse(community))---", fence = TRUE,
  lead = "The command lines are shown; the standalone <code>##</code> comment lines aren't -- running a comment just echoes it back and does nothing.")
```

```{r}
#| label: declared-count
#| include: false
# The count the sentence below quotes, from the loaded data (gated in prose-gates).
.sr_nmv <- sum(vapply(community, function(x)
  length(attr(x, "na_values")) > 0L || !is.null(attr(x, "na_range")), logical(1)))
```

`jload()` reports what it loaded. The report lists `r .sr_nmv` variables with
codes, such as -99 and -98, that stand for answers like "Refused" and "Don't
know"; it calls them SPSS-style missing values. jstats sets those codes aside in
every analysis, and so in every table: there is nothing to do about them here.
The report's closing lines, about base R and `jconvert()`, matter only if you
also analyze these data with base R's own functions. The tables on these pages
don't need that, so you can pass over those lines.
[Declaring missing values](missing-values.qmd) explains the codes.

### 2. Save a result

The first step is saving an analysis result in an *object*: R's word for
anything it keeps under a name, here the result of an analysis. R keeps an
object in its memory for the rest of the session; an object is not a file on
your computer. The **Environment** pane lists the objects you have. You make an
object with `<-`, the assignment operator from
[Step 3, RStudio Orientation](rstudio-orientation.qmd): the name on the left,
the analysis on the right. (Step 5, [jstats Quick Start](quickstart.qmd), saved
a regression this way, under the name `Results`.)

The name can be almost anything you like. These pages use short ones, `d1` for
descriptive statistics and `m1` for a model, but names like `descriptives1` or
`model_wellbeing` work just as well and may be easier to remember. A name can
contain letters, numbers, dots, and underscores. It must start with a letter,
and it can't contain a space or a dash, which R reads as a minus sign.
Capitalization has to match, as everywhere in R: `M1` and `m1` are two different
names.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
.obx$show_console(r"---(## ---- 2. Save a result -------------------------------------------------

## Save jdesc()'s result for three variables in an object named d1.
## The output still appears in the Console, as it would without d1 <-
d1 <- jdesc(Age, Income, WellbeingScore))---", fence = TRUE, env = TRUE)
```

The descriptive statistics appear in the Console as they would without
`d1 <-`, and the result is saved as well: `d1` is now in the **Environment**
pane, beside `community`. The pane lists what is in your workspace: the data you
loaded and the results you saved.

### 3. Save a second result without Console output

The result of any jstats analysis can be saved the same way. Save as many as you
like, each in an object of its own. When the Word table is all you want, add
`print = FALSE` inside the command's parentheses: the result is saved and
nothing appears in the Console. (In R, to *print* a result is to show it in the
Console. Nothing goes to a printer or to Word.) Here the second result is a
regression of the wellbeing score on age and income, saved as `m1`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
.obx$show_console(r"---(## ---- 3. Save a second result without Console output -------------------

## Save a regression in an object named m1. print = FALSE keeps the
## output out of the Console, since the Word table is what we're after
m1 <- jlm(WellbeingScore ~ Age + Income, print = FALSE))---", fence = TRUE, env = TRUE)
```

The Console shows the command and nothing else, and `m1` joins `d1` in the
**Environment** pane. The regression's output is saved with the result, though:
to see it after all, type `m1` in the Console.

### 4. Save a result in a file

An object is gone when the R session ends. To use a result in a later session,
save the result in a file. Give the result to `jsave()`, the same command that
saves a dataset in [Loading, Saving, Converting Data](data.qmd). For a result,
`jsave()` needs no file name: it names the file for the object, `m1.rds`. (The
`.rds` ending marks R's own file format.)

The block's second command then removes `m1` from the Environment with base R's
`rm()`. Ending the session would do the same to every object; removing `m1` now
lets block 5 show the result coming back from the file.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
.obx$show_console(r"---(## ---- 4. Save a result in a file ---------------------------------------

## Save the result m1 in a file. jsave() names the file m1.rds
jsave(m1)

## Remove m1 from the Environment, as ending the session would.
## rm() is base R, and shows nothing in the Console when it works
rm(m1)  # base R)---", fence = TRUE, env = TRUE, env_mark = "broom",
  note = "The red arrow points to the broom.")
```

```{r}
#| label: env-after-4
#| include: false
# What the Environment holds after block 4, and the file it wrote (gated in
# prose-gates, which runs at the foot).
.e4 <- ls(globalenv())
.f4 <- file.exists("m1.rds")
```

`jsave()` reports where it saved the file, with the file's full path, and gives
the command that loads the result back in a later session. On your screen the
path starts with your working directory (your project's folder), which this
page shows as `~/your-working-directory`. If you have set a data
folder, as [Loading, Saving, Converting Data](data.qmd) shows, the file is in
the data folder instead.

`rm()` shows nothing in the Console, and `m1` is gone from the **Environment**
pane, which now lists `community` and `d1`. The result is still in the file.

`rm()` removes the one object you name. To remove every object at once, click
the broom at the top of the **Environment** pane, where the red arrow points;
RStudio asks you to confirm first.

### 5. Load the result from the file

In a later session, load jstats, then load the result with `jload()`, the same
command that loads a dataset. Give `jload()` the result's name in quotes: it
reads the file `m1.rds` and puts the result in the Environment as `m1`. The
quotes are the one difference from block 4. There, `m1` was an object in the
Environment; here, `"m1"` is the name of a file, and in R a file's name goes in
quotes.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
.obx$show_console(r"---(## ---- 5. Load the result from the file ---------------------------------

## Load the result saved in m1.rds. It comes back as an object named m1
jload("m1"))---", fence = TRUE, env = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: env-after-5
#| include: false
# What the Environment holds after block 5 (gated in prose-gates).
.e5 <- ls(globalenv())
```

`jload()` reports where it found the file and what it loaded, and `m1` is back in
the **Environment** pane, beside `community` and `d1`. The loaded `m1` is the
result you saved: type `m1` in the Console to see the regression's output, or
give `m1` to `jtable()`. The file holds everything a table needs, so in a later
session the data do not have to be loaded first. Page 2, [Making a table in
Word](tables-in-word.qmd), makes a table from each result.

The file `m1.rds` stays in your folder until you delete it. The later pages
don't use the file, since each makes `d1` and `m1` again in its first block. To
delete the file, select its checkbox in the **Files** pane and click
**Delete**.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why jstats does it this way"}
Base R has two commands for this job: `saveRDS(m1, "m1.rds")` saves the result
in a file, and `m1 <- readRDS("m1.rds")` reads the file in a later session, the
name typed twice in each. The file is the same either way: `readRDS()` reads a
file that `jsave()` wrote, and `jload()` reads a file that `saveRDS()` wrote.

The base R commands do less around the file. `saveRDS()` shows nothing in the
Console, so it doesn't say where the file went. `saveRDS()` doesn't use your
data folder either: the folder has to be typed into the file name each time, as
in `"Data/m1.rds"`. And neither command asks first: `saveRDS()` replaces a file
of the same name, and `m1 <- readRDS("m1.rds")` replaces an `m1` you already
have. `jsave()` and `jload()` name the file for the object, report the full
path, use your data folder when you have set one, and ask before replacing a
file or an object.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Coming from SPSS, Stata, or SAS?"}
SPSS saves results by saving the Viewer's output in a file of its own, apart
from the data (`OUTPUT SAVE`). Stata saves a model's results with
`estimates save` and brings them back in a later session with `estimates use`.
`jsave()` and `jload()` do that job here, for the result of any jstats
analysis, and a loaded result still makes its table.
:::

```{r}
#| label: prose-gates
#| include: false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PROSE GATES -- hidden. Each stopifnot() below is one statement the prose
# makes about what the package does; a false one HALTS the render.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.pr <- function(x) utils::capture.output(print(x))
# block 1: jload()'s report names the declared codes, and the sentence's count.
# The report prints once a session, so it is read from a fresh R process.
.l1 <- callr::r(function() {
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(jstats))
  m <- character(0)
  o <- withCallingHandlers(utils::capture.output(jload("community")),
                           message = function(c) { m <<- c(m, conditionMessage(c))
                                                   invokeRestart("muffleMessage") })
  paste(c(m, o), collapse = "\n")
})
# block 2: the result prints, the same with and without the assignment
.l2a <- utils::capture.output(.y <- jdesc(Age, Income, WellbeingScore))
.l2b <- utils::capture.output(jdesc(Age, Income, WellbeingScore))
# block 3: nothing prints with print = FALSE
.q3 <- utils::capture.output(.z <- jlm(WellbeingScore ~ Age + Income, print = FALSE))
# block 3: typing m1 shows the regression's output after all (R85, v0.9.283)
.t3 <- .pr(m1)
.u3 <- utils::capture.output(jlm(WellbeingScore ~ Age + Income))
# block 4 (S429): jsave(m1) names the file for the object, in the working
# directory with no data folder set, and says so -- the path in full, what it
# is, the line that loads it back; rm(m1) left community and d1. Run again in
# a folder of its own, so the page's own file is not touched.
.notes <- function(expr) {   # a call's notes, in order
  m <- character(0)
  withCallingHandlers(expr, message = function(c) {
    m <<- c(m, conditionMessage(c)); invokeRestart("muffleMessage") })
  paste(m, collapse = "")
}
.g4 <- local({
  td <- tempfile("g4"); dir.create(td); .o <- setwd(td); on.exit(setwd(.o))
  e <- new.env(); e$m1 <- m1
  msg <- .notes(evalq(jsave(m1), e))
  list(msg = gsub("\\s+", " ", msg), td = normalizePath(td, winslash = "/"),
       file = file.exists("m1.rds"),
       out = utils::capture.output(saveRDS(m1, "base.rds")),
       base_msg = .notes(saveRDS(m1, "base2.rds")))
})
# block 4: with a data folder set the file goes there, and saveRDS() does
# not use the folder; read in a fresh R session, as a reader's later one.
.m1f <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds"); saveRDS(m1, .m1f)
.g4d <- callr::r(function(f) {
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(jstats))
  td <- tempfile("g4d"); dir.create(td); setwd(td)
  m1 <- readRDS(f)
  joptions(data.dir = "Data", quiet = TRUE)
  invisible(utils::capture.output(suppressMessages(jsave(m1))))
  saveRDS(m1, "base.rds")
  list(jsave_in_data = file.exists(file.path("Data", "m1.rds")),
       jsave_in_wd = file.exists("m1.rds"),
       base_in_wd = file.exists("base.rds"),
       base_in_data = file.exists(file.path("Data", "base.rds")),
       again = tryCatch({ suppressMessages(jsave(m1)); "saved" },
                        error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)))
}, args = list(f = .m1f))
# block 5: jload("m1") reads the file back under its name, said in one line;
# in a fresh session, with no data loaded, the loaded result makes the same
# table as the result in memory.
.g5 <- local({
  td <- tempfile("g5"); dir.create(td); .o <- setwd(td); on.exit(setwd(.o))
  file.copy(file.path(.o, "m1.rds"), "m1.rds")
  e <- new.env()
  msg <- .notes(evalq(jload("m1"), e))
  e$m1 <- 1
  replaced <- .notes(evalq(jload("m1"), e))
  list(msg = gsub("\\s+", " ", msg), back = exists("m1", envir = e, inherits = FALSE),
       replaced = gsub("\\s+", " ", replaced), now = class(e$m1))
})
.g5t <- callr::r(function(f) {
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(jstats))
  td <- tempfile("g5t"); dir.create(td); setwd(td); file.copy(f, "m1.rds")
  suppressMessages(jload("m1"))
  # no data frame in the session: jload() assigns here, in the function's
  # frame, and nothing is in the global environment (community is the
  # package's own, reached through the search path, never loaded)
  held <- c(mget(ls(), envir = environment()), mget(ls(globalenv()), envir = globalenv()))
  list(no_data = !any(vapply(held, is.data.frame, logical(1))), loaded = exists("m1", inherits = FALSE),
       table = utils::capture.output(print(jtable(m1, print = FALSE))))
}, args = list(f = .m1f))
# the box: readRDS() reads the file jsave() wrote, jload() a file saveRDS()
# wrote; saveRDS() replaces a file of the same name without a word.
.gb <- local({
  td <- tempfile("gb"); dir.create(td); .o <- setwd(td); on.exit(setwd(.o))
  saveRDS(m1, "s.rds"); e <- new.env()
  invisible(.notes(evalq(jload("s"), e)))
  a <- readRDS(file.path(.o, "m1.rds"))
  saveRDS(d1, "x.rds"); out2 <- utils::capture.output(saveRDS(m1, "x.rds"))
  list(read = .pr(jtable(a, print = FALSE)), loaded = .pr(jtable(e$s, print = FALSE)),
       replaced = inherits(readRDS("x.rds"), "jst_lm"), silent = length(out2) == 0L)
})
unlink(.m1f)
stopifnot(
  grepl(paste(.sr_nmv, "variables have SPSS-style missing values"), .l1, fixed = TRUE),
  grepl('-99 ["Refused"]', .l1, fixed = TRUE), grepl('-98 ["Don\'t know"]', .l1, fixed = TRUE),
  grepl("Base R functions do not", .l1, fixed = TRUE),
  grepl("jconvert(community", .l1, fixed = TRUE),
  length(.l2a) > 0L, identical(.l2a, .l2b), length(.q3) == 0L,
  inherits(d1, "jst_desc"), inherits(m1, "jst_lm"),
  all(c("community", "d1", "m1") %in% ls(globalenv())),
  length(.t3) > 5L, identical(.t3, .u3), grepl("Linear Regression", .t3[1], fixed = TRUE),
  # block 4
  .f4, setequal(.e4, c("community", "d1")),
  .g4$file, startsWith(.g4$msg, paste0("Saved m1 to ", .g4$td, "/m1.rds ")),
  grepl("(R format; a jlm() result)", .g4$msg, fixed = TRUE),
  grepl('To load it in a later session: jload("m1")', .g4$msg, fixed = TRUE),
  length(.g4$out) == 0L, identical(.g4$base_msg, ""),
  .g4d$jsave_in_data, !.g4d$jsave_in_wd, .g4d$base_in_wd, !.g4d$base_in_data,
  grepl("this file already exists", .g4d$again, fixed = TRUE),
  # block 5
  setequal(.e5, c("community", "d1", "m1")), inherits(m1, "jst_lm"),
  .g5$back, grepl("Loaded m1 (R format; a jlm() result made by jstats ", .g5$msg, fixed = TRUE),
  startsWith(.g5$msg, "Found m1.rds in "),
  grepl("already existed and has been replaced", .g5$replaced, fixed = TRUE),
  identical(.g5$now, class(m1)),
  .g5t$no_data, .g5t$loaded,
  identical(.g5t$table, .pr(jtable(m1, print = FALSE))),
  # the box
  identical(.gb$read, .pr(jtable(m1, print = FALSE))),
  identical(.gb$loaded, .pr(jtable(m1, print = FALSE))),
  .gb$replaced, .gb$silent
)
```

## Take the whole script with you

That's the full run-through. If you'd like the entire script in one file to
keep and reuse, download it here. Put your own analyses in place of the two on
this page, each saved under a name of its own.

The file is the finished version of the script you built: the same code, in the
same order. If you run the file a second time in the same session, `jload()`
asks before replacing `community`. `jsave()` asks before replacing the file
`m1.rds` whenever that file is already in your folder. The file's first lines
say what to answer.
[Using the How-To pages](howtos.qmd#using-the-how-to-pages) says more about
finished scripts and how to run one.

.sr_clean()
